This petition coming on for admission this day, Hon'ble 
 Vishal Mishra passed the following:
 Order

This petition is filed seeking the following reliefs :-
"

(i ) The Hon'ble Court kindly be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus to quash the order impugned dated 07.02.2022 & 07.10.2022 (Annexure P/3)and entire land acquisition proceeding and it notification if any, in the interest of justice.
( i i )
The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent authority to restore the acquired agricultural land in the name of petitioners in its original structures, in the interest of justice.

OR The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent authority to calculate proper valuation and provide service minimum one person in each family and also provide similar area of agriculture land in another place, in the interest of justice.

2. It is the case of the petitioners that the agriculture lands of their ownership which were allotted to their ancestors almost in the year 1968-69 by the Government for rehabilitation to survive, have been directed to be acquired under the WCL Policy for the purpose of coal mining/road widening.

The petitioners jointly and severally objected to the Revenue Authority against the proposed acquisition on the ground that without any prior notice/notification and knowledge the entire action of acquisition is taking place.
Vide order dated 07.10.2022, the private lands belonging to the petitioners have been mutated in the name of WCL in Khasra year 2022-23.
It is their case that petitioners are still in possession of the remaining land but the acquired land has been mutated without following the mandatory provisions of the M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959.
It is argued that the entire proceedings are contrary to Section 41 of the Land Acquisition Act and land cannot be acquired for private company so far as WCL is concerned.
Therefore, the present petition has been filed.

3. From perusal of the record, it is seen that the petitioners have not challenged the initial notification which has been issued for acquisition of the land in question nor the said notification is brought on record in the writ petition.
The claim raised by the petitioners is after the entire acquisition proceedings are completed even the name of the WCL has been mutated in the revenue records.
Challenge is made on the ground that no notices were issued to the petitioners but the fact remains that the acquisition of the land is in the knowledge of the petitioners.
The same is reflected from the fact that they themselves have stated in the petition that they are in possession of the part of the land.
They have challenged the mutation proceedings.
Under these circumstances, it cannot be said that the petitioners were not having any knowledge about the mutation proceedings.

The entire proceedings have been done in terms of Section 9(1) of Koyla Dharak Kshetra Adhiniyam,
1957.

The order dated 07.02.2022 clearly indicates that the amount of compensation has been ascertained by the Authorities and as far as rehabilitation is concerned, the amount has been calculated by the authorities and the persons who are displaced are required to be paid Rs.5,00,000/- each and the families which are required to be rehabilitated are required to pay Rs.5,00,000/- per family.
At such a belated stage the petitioners have approached the Court and that too without challenging the initial notification issued for acquisition of the land.
Under these circumstances, no relief can be extended to the petitioner.
4. The writ petition sans merit and is accordingly dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(RAVI MALIMATH) (V  CHIEF JUSTICE   AM Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90027686/
